title: Extensions and maintenance
goal: Design an original teaching extension and verify compatibility and disabling.
prerequisites: onec.p11; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Dependencies, hashes and own changes are explicit.
Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: An extension develops a solution within defined boundaries without uncontrolled base edits. State borrowed objects and modified methods. Use an original course configuration, not a proprietary standard solution. Avoiding direct base edits does not eliminate risks to data or behavior.

Keep base configuration, extension and data separate. Restore an accepted own DT into a new directory. Open Designer → Configuration → Configuration extensions → Add, choose an own training name and inspect purpose/compatibility version. Use no third-party extension.

Bind the extension to exact base version, compatibility mode and source hash. Changes to borrowed methods can invalidate assumptions after an upgrade. Do not claim all-future compatibility. List accepted, rejected and untested combinations; similar build numbers do not transferPASS.

Choose a minimal change without data migration: an own command explaining minute units on the training form. Borrow the needed form/object through the extension editor and retain the borrowed-object list/source. Do not replace the original document UUID or copy an entire configuration for one command.

Disabling an extension changes behavior and can affect access to its data. Identify extension-owned fields and records first. Never test disabling on the only work. Preserve a backup, base-only version and an independent extended copy; test reenabling too.

Add an own client action to the extended form: Сообщить("Длительность указывается в минутах; запись выполняется отдельно."); bind the command and place it on the bar. Save/apply in the copy and open the same request. The command shows its hint; old values/actions keep working.

Add a simple workflow rule, such as priority validation, with positive/negative cases. Compare baseline behavior, disable on a copy and verify return. Declare original contributions and the base used: executing a package proves neither authorship nor distribution rights over others’code.

Export only the own CFE and source. Disable it in the experiment copy: its command disappears while requests/durations remain. This minimal example adds no extension-owned data; removing a data-bearing extension needs a separate migration/rollback plan. Check compatibility per new version.
